text:
Recent work supports learning temporal boundaries rather than imposing fixed session thresholds. [TiSRec (RecSys 2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3759327) dynamically partitions histories into Local Preference Blocks using significant time intervals, then models within-block and between-block preferences. [Session-aware recommendation (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109) explores lightweight session tokens, segment embeddings and temporal attention. [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuously evolving interests and interval-dependent uncertainty. These provide motivation for temporal conditioning, but do not establish that elapsed time identifies intent or satisfied needs.

For NextItNet, a practical research hypothesis is a jointly trained gate on each causal convolution tap, conditioned on log elapsed time and differences between current and historical hidden states. This could suppress evidence across likely preference changes while retaining older relevant interactions; it adapts the effective receptive field directly, without averaging network depths. Preserve the residual path and causal masking, and compare content-only, time-only and combined gates. [Original NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) supplies the dilated causal backbone; the proposed temporal tap gate is an extrapolation, not a verified published NextItNet result. Searches found no direct 2023–2026 match demonstrating this exact mechanism. Use only observed history timestamps, require timestamp availability at inference, and assess gains through the fixed macro validation HR@10 with one jointly trained model per category.
